risks.note: Management's Risks, Threats and Concerns section flags that while branded generics account for the vast majority of India's pharmaceutical market by value, trade generics have grown rapidly. With maximum retail prices similar to branded generics but free of the cost of promotion to doctors, trade generics manufacturers have room to offer higher margins and discounts to stockists and retailers - a direct threat to a company whose entire moat rests on prescriber promotion. IQVIA India estimates trade generics accounted for around 12% of the total market in value terms in 2025.
risks.risk: Trade generics eroding the branded-generic model

risks.note: The Company operated solely within the pharmaceuticals segment for the year under review, and 100% of turnover comes from a single activity - wholesale trading of pharmaceutical and medical goods. It owns no manufacturing facilities, so it depends entirely on third-party and related-party supply for product, leaving no internal lever over cost, quality or continuity of supply.
risks.risk: Single-segment, single-activity concentration with no manufacturing base

risks.note: BRSR openness-of-business disclosures show 98.8% of sales go to dealers and distributors, and the top 10 dealers/distributors account for 60.8% of total sales to that channel. The distributor count also fell to 1,762 from 1,978, so the channel is both concentrated and narrowing, giving a small number of intermediaries material bargaining power.

Purchases from related parties were 48.4% of total purchases, up from 41.3% in the prior year, with stock-in-trade sourced from a fellow Novartis subsidiary. Following the change in control on July 29, 2026, when the Company ceased to be part of the Novartis Global Group, the continuity and commercial terms of this supply relationship become a structural uncertainty.

Under the SPA dated February 19, 2026 Novartis AG sold 70.68% of share capital to WaveRise Investments, ChrysCapital Fund X and Two Infinity Partners, closing July 29, 2026. The Company must now stand up independent finance, compliance, supply chain and technology functions that were previously group-provided, and the Board withheld the FY 2025-26 dividend to preserve flexibility during the transaction period, indicating the transition constrains capital-return policy.
risks.risk: Change of control and separation from the Novartis Group

risks.note: MD&A notes prices of APIs, solvents and intermediates have risen sharply on higher oil prices, restricted vessel movement and tightening shipping capacity, raising freight costs and delaying sourcing. A large share of pharmaceutical inputs derive from petrochemicals and India imports a significant proportion of APIs, so these trends feed directly into procurement cost and could pressure margins if sustained.
risks.risk: Input cost inflation and imported-API exposure

risks.note: The rupee has weakened to near-record lows against the US dollar on higher oil import bills, a widening trade deficit and capital outflows, with gradual depreciation expected to persist. The Company's exports are NIL, so it earns no foreign-currency revenue to offset the cost of imported and related-party sourced product - an unhedged structural mismatch.
risks.risk: Currency depreciation on an import-linked cost base with nil exports

currentContext.expansion: Novartis India Limited is an asset-light business with no manufacturing capex programme: the BRSR states the Company is engaged in trading and distribution of pharmaceutical products and does not have any manufacturing facilities, with nil plants and a national footprint of seven offices comprising one corporate office in Mumbai and six warehousing locations across Mumbai, Haryana, Kolkata, Chennai and Ghaziabad, serving 22 states. Expansion is therefore commercial rather than physical. The principal initiative is the consolidation of full commercial control of four flagship brands - Voveran, Methergin, Macalvit and Calcium Sandoz - bringing them fully back under NIL as part of the FY 2026-27 transition, which management describes as strengthening direct control over commercialisation, pricing and lifecycle decisions. Beyond this, the stated growth agenda is to expand the portfolio through new launches and selective in-licensing of differentiated therapies in white spaces, to pursue disciplined therapy-aligned acquisitions and integration drawing on a capital-light balance sheet, and to deepen last-mile distribution reach into tier 2 and tier 3 markets where specialist franchises remain under-penetrated. Organisational build-out includes a structured talent management framework for field and medical teams, early investment in data and analytics for field deployment, prescriber engagement and demand forecasting, embedding artificial intelligence into workflows across commercial, supply chain and compliance, and building independent high-governance functions across finance, compliance, supply chain and technology as the Company stands up on its own following the change of control that closed on July 29, 2026. The BRSR discloses no R&D or capex investment in technologies to improve environmental and social impacts in either the current or previous financial year.

Following the change in control on July 29, 2026, when the Company ceased to be part of the Novartis Global Group, the continuity and commercial terms of this supply relationship become a structural uncertainty.
- Under the SPA dated February 19, 2026 Novartis AG sold 70.68% of share capital to WaveRise Investments, ChrysCapital Fund X and Two Infinity Partners, closing July 29, 2026. The Company must now stand up independent finance, compliance, supply chain and technology functions that were previously group-provided, and the Board withheld the FY 2025-26 dividend to preserve flexibility during the transaction period, indicating the transition constrains capital-return policy.
- MD&A notes prices of APIs, solvents and intermediates have risen sharply on higher oil prices, restricted vessel movement and tightening shipping capacity, raising freight costs and delaying sourcing. A large share of pharmaceutical inputs derive from petrochemicals and India imports a significant proportion of APIs, so these trends feed directly into procurement cost and could pressure margins if sustained.
- The rupee has weakened to near-record lows against the US dollar on higher oil import bills, a widening trade deficit and capital outflows, with gradual depreciation expected to persist. The Company's exports are NIL, so it earns no foreign-currency revenue to offset the cost of imported and related-party sourced product - an unhedged structural mismatch.
- The updated Uniform Code for Pharmaceutical Marketing Practices, mandatory from March 2024, emphasises executive accountability, limits promotional items and samples and constrains engagement with medical practitioners - shifting the basis of prescriber engagement on which the Company's brand equity depends. Several tax and indirect-tax matters also remain under appeal, including a transfer-pricing draft order, a service-tax demand and a TDS demand.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- STRENGTHEN: deepen specialist engagement and sharpen medical outreach across the flagship brands that have earned decades of prescriber loyalty
- EXPAND: launch and selectively in-license differentiated therapies in white spaces
- ACQUIRE: pursue disciplined, therapy-aligned acquisitions and integration, drawing on a capital-light balance sheet
- EXCEL: build independent, high-governance functions across finance, compliance, supply chain and technology as the Company stands up on its own
- Consolidate full commercial control of four flagship brands - Voveran, Methergin, Macalvit and Calcium Sandoz - …
